notes: The *both … and* of the closing coordination is distributed across the two written waws (s027, s031) rather than given whole to one, since each coordinated member has a connective morpheme of its own — rule 14's `אוֹ … אוֹ` case, with two connectives counted against two English words. The whole-pair reading is named in that unit's note.
s025 (לְ of לָכֶם) is unrepresented because the ASV recasts the clause as *ye shall have*: הָיָה takes the *have* and the suffix the subject pronoun (rules 40, 43).
Both construct chains write a *the* before each word, so rule 29's arthrous case governs: the present article takes the *the* before its own word and the construct noun a supplied one.
אֶזְרַח → *him that is born* keeps the supplied antecedent, relative and copula in the substantive's own unit under rules 46 and 20, headed on *born*.
